department: Department of Applied Science (Applied Mathematics and Statistics Emphasis)

deadline.value: No separate Applied Science deadline is published; under Policy LR 509.9 (revised April 2026) and Graduate School International Prospects, all international application materials for Fall must be received by June 1 (June 1, 2027 inferred for Fall 2027; Spring Oct 1; Summer March 1). Note: the 2026-2027 catalog also prints legacy general international dates of July 1 and Feb 1.
deadline.quote: Application materials must be received no later than June 1 for fall semester, October 1 for spring semester, and March 1 for summer semester.

also.quote: Fall applications: June 1 | Spring applications: October 1 | Summer applications: March 1
They must be received no later than July 1 for the fall semester and November 1 for the spring semester, and March 1 for the summer semester.

gre_general.value: GRE General is required (min 155Q, 138V, 4.5 AW in the 2026-2027 catalog; the program Steps to Apply page states 300 combined and 4.5 AW), except applicants with a 3.5+ GPA on their last 60 credit hours may be exempted with graduate coordinator approval.
gre_general.quote: Official GRE General Test from ETS (UA Little Rock’s institutional code is 6368) | Applicants with a 3.5 or greater GPA on their last 60 credit hours are not required to take the GRE.

also.quote: On the GRE, applicants must have a minimum quantitative score of 155, a verbal score of at least 138, and a writing assessment score of at least 4.5 | With the approval of the graduate coordinator, applicants with a 3.5 GPA or greater on their last 60 graduate and undergraduate credit hours, may not be required to take the GRE.

gre_subject.value: Neither the catalog nor the program page states whether the ETS GRE Mathematics Subject Test is required, optional, or not considered (only GRE General requirements are stated).

supervisor.value: Admission is made with the collective input of Applied Science Doctoral faculty (faculty mentor availability is considered), and entering students complete a mandatory first-semester Laboratory Rotation (ASCI 7450X) to select a dissertation advisor.
supervisor.quote: Recommendations on a doctoral application for admission to the Applied Science program are made with the collective input of the Applied Science Doctoral faculty. | All Applied Science doctoral students must register for Introduction to Research in Applied Science (ASCI 7450X), also called “Laboratory Rotation,” in their first semester in the program

funding.value: Funding is limited and not guaranteed with admission; admission and funding decisions are separate. Full-time doctoral GAs/TAs/RAs receive a minimum $15,000 9-month stipend (effective Fall 2026), 9 credits of tuition waiver per semester, and $400/semester health insurance reimbursement, renewable each semester with >=3.0 GPA.
funding.quote: Admission decisions and funding decisions are considered separately, and the number of students admitted is usually much higher than the number of students who are funded. There are a limited number of funding opportunities and funding is not guaranteed to all students.

also.quote: The full-time stipend for the academic year is a minimum of $15,000 for doctoral students and $10,000 for master’s students. | Full-time Graduate Assistants must be enrolled in at least 9 hours of credit courses that are covered by the tuition waiver.
The Doctoral Health Insurance Reimbursement provides $400 of insurance reimbursement for Fall and another $400 for Spring.
Doctoral-level graduate assistants will see their minimum stipend increase from $13,000 to $15,000.

entry_route.value: Requires a baccalaureate degree in an appropriate scientific discipline with at least 3.0 overall GPA (catalog) or 3.3 on the last 60 credit hours (Steps to Apply page); 72 credit hours beyond the bachelor's degree. Requires prerequisite preparation in discrete math, single/multivariable calculus, linear algebra, differential equations, mathematical statistics, and programming through data structures.
entry_route.quote: Applicants must possess a baccalaureate degree in an appropriate scientific discipline such as chemistry, physics, materials science, biology, mathematics, statistics, or earth science. | All emphases require a minimum of 72 credit hours beyond the baccalaureate degree.

notes: Applied Science, Applied Mathematics and Statistics, Ph.D. (catalog poid=5497). Covers both Applied Mathematics and Applied Statistics candidacy/research areas (mapped to math + also_fields: statistics). Non-native English speakers qualifying for a TA must score 5.0 on TSE.
